tutorial.title: Aligning Flex Items
tutorial.descriptionContent: Learn how to align flex items alongside the cross axis.

lessons.title: Lesson #1
lessons.interactiveContent:
Let's learn how to align HUD items along the cross axis.

Try the buttons to see how a game HUD layout can change.

lessons.title: Lesson #2
lessons.interactiveContent:
To align HUD items along the cross axis, we use align-items.

Make sure to pick align-items.

lessons.title: Lesson #3
lessons.interactiveContent:
The default align-items value is stretch. It makes HUD items fill the entire cross axis.

Make sure to pick stretch.

lessons.title: Lesson #4
lessons.interactiveContent:
With flex-direction: column, stretch makes items fill the container width (cross axis is horizontal).

Make sure to pick column, followed by stretch.

lessons.title: Lesson #5
lessons.interactiveContent:
flex-start keeps items at their content size and places them at the start of the cross axis.

Make sure to pick flex-start.

lessons.title: Lesson #6
lessons.interactiveContent:
flex-end pushes items to the end of the cross axis.

Make sure to pick flex-end.

lessons.title: Lesson #7
lessons.interactiveContent:
To center HUD items inside the container, we use center.

Make sure to pick center.

lessons.title: Lesson #8
lessons.interactiveContent: Try different flex-direction and align-items settings to see how a game HUD adapts.

lessons.title: Lesson #9
lessons.interactiveContent:
What happens when we use align-items?

Items are aligned based on the cross axisItems are aligned based on the main axis

Items are aligned based on the cross axis.

lessons.title: Lesson #10
lessons.interactiveContent:
What is the default value for align-items?

stretchflex-start

Make sure to pick stretch.

lessons.title: Lesson #11
lessons.interactiveContent:
Why do HUD items fill the container horizontally when flex-direction is column?

Because the cross axis is horizontal and items stretch by defaultBecause align-items is set to center

Because the cross axis is horizontal and items stretch by default.

lessons.title: Lesson #12
lessons.interactiveContent:
What align-items value does this HUD use?

flex-startcenter

Make sure to pick flex-start.

lessons.title: Lesson #13
lessons.interactiveContent:
What align-items value does this HUD use?

flex-endspace-around

Make sure to pick flex-end.

lessons.title: Lesson #14
lessons.interactiveContent:
What align-items value does this HUD use?

centerflex-end

Make sure to pick center.

lessons.title: Lesson #15
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the align-items property.

Make sure to pick align, followed by -, and finally items.

lessons.title: Lesson #16
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code the default align-items value, stretch.

Make sure to type stretch.

lessons.title: Lesson #17
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code flex-start.

Make sure to pick flex, followed by -, and finally start.

lessons.title: Lesson #18
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code flex-end.

Make sure to pick flex, followed by -, and finally end.

lessons.title: Lesson #19
lessons.interactiveContent:
Code align-items: center.

Make sure to pick align followed by - and then items, center.

lessons.title: Lesson #20
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set flex-direction to column and align-items to stretch.

Make sure to pick column, followed by stretch.

lessons.title: Lesson #21
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set align-items to flex-start.

Make sure to pick flex, followed by -, and finally start.

lessons.title: Lesson #22
lessons.interactiveContent:
Set align-items to flex-end.

Make sure to pick flex, followed by -, and finally end.
